title: Gray-release KV-cache cross-variant contamination causing rollback pinlock
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: During a gray-release of model version v2.5 we observed elevated 5xx rates and high latency for a subset of hosts. Investigation found cross-variant pollution of KV caches when requests were routed to pooled serving processes that briefly hosted different model variants. The contamination caused cache misses and application-level errors that triggered the rollout controller to attempt a rollback, but version pin state became inconsistent between control-plane and edge proxies, leaving traffic pinned to a failing variant (pinlock). This ticket documents the incident, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-01T07:14Z a gradual gray-release for model v2.5 introduced a subtle KV cache namespace collision when our serving pool reused processes across variant changes. Affected servers served mixed KV entries which caused model context/tokenization mismatches and an elevated error rate. Automated rollback attempted at 07:42Z encountered inconsistent version pin metadata across regions, producing a stuck rollback (pinlock) until manual intervention at 09:08Z. Impact: ~18% increased p50/p95 latency for affected routes, 12k failed requests over 1.5 hours, outage for customers using dedicated routes in us-west-2 for ~1.9 hours.
timeline:
2026-03-01 07:14Z - Gray-release v2.5 started (10% traffic).
2026-03-01 07:28Z - Ops alerted via SLO paging for increased error rate on /generate.
2026-03-01 07:35Z - Initial triage: increased KV-cache miss rate and "payload parse" errors on specific hosts.
2026-03-01 07:42Z - Rollout controller started automated rollback.
2026-03-01 07:50Z - Some edge proxies reported mismatched pinned_version vs control-plane desired_version.
2026-03-01 08:10Z - Rollback did not converge; traffic split still routing to v2.5 in some AZs.
2026-03-01 08:45Z - Manual orchestration: pin overridden on control plane and failing hosts drained.
2026-03-01 09:08Z - Traffic restored to stable variant v2.4. Post-incident monitoring continued until 11:00Z.
root_cause: 1) Serving pool reuses long-lived processes across variant swaps; process-local KV cache keys were not fully namespaced by model build id + variant tag. 2) Gray-release path performs quick variant attach/detach without a full per-process cache flush on variant change. 3) Rollout controller and edge proxies have eventual-consistency reconciliation windows; a race when rollback was triggered left control-plane pin metadata inconsistent with proxies (stale route cache TTLs + no forced re-sync). 4) Lack of a safety interlock that prevents rollbacks when KV cache warming state indicates cross-variant contamination.
mitigations:
- Immediate: Drained and reprovisioned affected hosts; forced control-plane pin override and proxy cache invalidation commands to restore routing (manual runbook).
- Short-term: Disable gray-release for v2.5 until hotfix landed; deployed patch to gate reuse of process-local KV cache across variant attach.
- Monitoring: Added dashboard for per-host KV cache miss rate and tag-entropy metric to detect mixed-variant cache contents early.
action_items: A1: Add per-process KV cache namespace that includes model_build_id and variant_id (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-15)
A2: Implement safe-attach flow: on variant attach, require cache flush or private warming container before serving mixed traffic (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 8, due: 2026-03-22)

A3: Rollout controller improvement: add 'rollback atomicity' gate that verifies proxy pin convergence before allowing automated rollback to mark complete (owner: Daniel Chen, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-18)
A4: Edge proxy: add forced pin re-sync endpoint and make controller call it during rollback; log idempotent ack (owner: Elena Park, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-14)
A5: Runbook: update 'stuck-rollback' playbook with steps to force drain, proxy re-sync, and validate cache namespaces (owner: On-call, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-05)
A6: Add invariant tests in staging that simulate variant swap and ensure no cross-variant KV read observed (owner: QA automation, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-25)
A7: Add alert: 'per-host kv-entropy > 1' to trigger early investigation and circuit breaker to pause gray-releases (owner: SRE, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-12)
A8: Post-incident retro: schedule blameless review with product/infra to decide longer-term architecture for cache scoping (owner: Sofia Martinez, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-10)
A9: Backfill: Audit other codepaths that reuse process-local caches (owner: Daniel Chen, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-30)
A10: Bake a canary pre-check in the console that runs an isolation test verifying cache correctness before opening traffic to new variant (owner: Product Console, estimate: 8, due: 2026-04-05)
A11: Customer communications: prepare and send post-incident summary to affected customers with timeline and mitigations (owner: Customer Success - Maya Patel, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-06)
comments: 2026-03-01 Sofia Martinez: Initial page received. Triage team confirmed elevated 5xx and observed parse errors tied to tokenization mismatch. Starting rollback.
2026-03-01 Daniel Chen: Noticing per-host cache key collisions in logs. Collecting heapdumps and KV entries. Suspect namespace leak when process is attached to new variant without flush.

2026-03-01 Marcus Lee: Deployed provisional guard that prevents immediate reuse of process after detach; this reduced error spike but rollback still stuck in two AZs. Need control-plane > proxy sync fix.

2026-03-01 Elena Park: Implemented proxy cache invalidation via admin endpoint; manual run used to converge pins. Filed PR to make this callable by rollout controller: github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/1287
2026-03-03 Priya Singh: Added unit tests for KV namespace generation and found several edge cases in lower-level cache code. Will push fix this week. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4532

2026-03-10 Marcus Lee: Performance trade-off note: Namespacing caches increases memory overhead by ~6% in p99 host memory; we must consider memory pressure in Dedicated pools. Will propose a memory cap + eviction policy in follow-up.
2026-03-11 Sofia Martinez: Retro scheduled for 2026-03-12. Invitees: infra, runtime, rollout-controller, SRE, product console, CS.
